Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
• 35-40 y/o man with 3-day history of watery diarrhoea (6–7 ×/day) plus intermittent left-lower-abdominal cramps after recent takeaway meal; clinical picture most consistent with acute viral or bacterial gastroenteritis.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Loose, watery stools ×3 days, frequency 6–7/day.  
• Timeline/progression: Abrupt onset the morning after eating takeaway (Chinese) 4 days ago; ongoing but not worsening.  
• Associated symptoms: Intermittent cramping left-sided abdominal pain, initial vomiting (now resolved), subjective fever on day 1, weakness/shakiness, loss of appetite; able to maintain oral fluids.  
• Pertinent negatives: No visible blood or mucus in stool or vomit; no persistent vomiting, melena, night sweats.  
• Past medical history: Well-controlled asthma.  
• Allergies: Not discussed.  
• Medications: Inhaler only (type not specified).  
• Social / preventive: Married with two children (one child vomited once); accountant; non-smoker; does not consume alcohol.

Examination:
• Telehealth visit – no vitals or physical exam performed.  
• No visual evidence of distress reported by clinician.

Impression:
• Most likely diagnosis: Acute viral gastroenteritis – fits abrupt onset, watery diarrhoea, short course, household contact with mild symptoms.  
• Alternate considerations:  
  – Acute bacterial food-borne infection (Salmonella/Campylobacter/ETEC) – possible given takeaway meal and feverish feeling, but lack of blood and no similar illness in meal companions lowers likelihood.  
  – Diverticulitis with diarrhoea – less likely; pain intermittent, patient appears young, stool volume > pain, no systemic red flags.

Plan:
• Conservative management:  
  – Oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte) to maintain fluids and electrolytes.  
  – Paracetamol 1 g (two 500 mg tablets) up to QID PRN for fever or discomfort.  
  – Light diet as tolerated; continue soups/smoothies.  
• Activity: Recommend 2–3 days off work to rest and limit spread.  
• Red-flag advice / follow-up:  
  – Return or seek urgent review if bloody stools, persistent vomiting, inability to keep fluids down, high fever, severe or worsening abdominal pain.  
  – Reassessment in 3–4 days if diarrhoea not improving; consider stool culture and further investigations at that time.  
• No antibiotics indicated at present.

Quality checks
● Missing expected elements: Exact age, allergies, inhaler specifics, baseline vitals, vaccination status, formal follow-up appointment date.  
● Conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Clear but informal; no physical exam or vitals due to teleconsult; some minor repetitions.
